# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** MVP Health Care — Member Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Cameron Brooks
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-13 — Reference number POC-5EDC35C98D-81118**
- **Member:** Cameron Brooks
- **Member ID:** W412154328
- **Plan:** MVP Health Care (Commercial/ACA), State of Vermont
- **Service denied:** Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
- **Governing policy I am citing:** *MVP Health Care 2025 Annual Notices for Providers (NY)*, https://www.mvphealthcare.com/-/media/project/mvp/healthcare/documents/legal/2025-annual-notices-providers-ny.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing MVP's denial of the knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881) requested by my surgeon, Duval, MD. I am asking MVP to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure. The notice states that the request was denied because the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. My records show a long and well-documented course of conservative treatment, and I am asking that they be reviewed again in full.

## The plan's own stated policy on medical necessity

The policy I have been given states:

> "Medical Management Decisions It is the policy of MVP to provide coverage for medically necessary health care services provided to our Members."

It also describes how those decisions are made:

> "Utilization Management Criteria MVP uses the most current version of InterQual ® criteria as a guideline for its utilization management decisions for inpatient services and certain medical services."

I want to be straightforward with the reviewer about one thing: the InterQual criteria are not public, and I have not been given the specific criteria text that was applied to my case. So I am not quoting any conservative-care requirement here, because **no such threshold — no required number of weeks, visits, injections, or months of medication — appears anywhere in the policy language I have.** The policy text available to me also includes sections that end in a colon and introduce lists that were not reproduced in what I received, so I am aware that further conditions exist in the policy that I have not seen. Rather than guess at the standard, I am setting out the facts in my records and asking MVP to identify the exact criterion it used.

## What my records document

The plan's own record standards speak directly to the value of a thorough, continuous chart:

> "MVP Medical Record Standards and Guidelines Well-documented electronic or paper medical records improve communication and promote coordination and continuity of care."

and

> "Unresolved problems from previous office visits should be addressed and documented in subsequent visits."

My chart is exactly that kind of record. It documents a problem that was treated non-surgically, revisited over many months, and did not resolve:

| What the plan's decision questions | What my records state |
|---|---|
| Duration of the problem | 12 months of progressive pain in the knee, unrelieved by rest |
| Supervised physical therapy | Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, 14 weeks, from 2026-04-08 to 2026-07-15, **24 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note |
| Medication trial | NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief |
| Injection | Corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-10, giving 4 weeks of partial relief |
| Imaging | MRI of the knee, 2026-07-02: displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking; articular cartilage preserved, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 |
| Physical examination | Positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain |
| Function | Locking and giving way; cannot squat or kneel; limited to level walking |
| Safety / surgical candidacy | No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker |

This is a course of conservative care that was tried, documented, and completed — physical therapy through discharge, eight months of anti-inflammatory medication, and a steroid injection — and it did not relieve the problem. My MRI documents a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking, and my exam and function notes record locking and giving way, and an inability to squat or kneel. My surgeon, Duval, MD, has documented that this procedure is needed.

## Request for the criteria MVP applied

The policy states that criteria are available on request:

> "MVP Members may request a copy of the criteria used to make a specific utilization management determination by contacting the MVP Customer Care Center at the number on the back of their MVP Member ID card."

and

> "Providers may request a copy of the criteria employed to make a specific utilization management determination by contacting the MVP Utilization Management Department at 1-800-568-0458 ."

I am making that request now, in writing, and I am asking for it in writing in return. **Please provide me, free of charge, the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, along with any internal rule or guideline relied on to conclude that my conservative treatment was inadequate. Federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules entitle me to the specific rule or criterion the plan relied on in denying my claim. MVP holds those criteria; I do not. Without them I cannot see which requirement my 24 documented physical therapy visits, 8 months of NSAIDs, and steroid injection are said to fall short of — and neither can a reviewer checking this appeal.

I would also note, from the plan's own description of its review structure:

> "MMC Membership includes practicing Providers from representative specialties, including at least one Provider from each region within the MVP service area, and health plan staff."

I ask that my appeal be reviewed by a physician in orthopedic surgery or a comparable specialty, given the specific nature of the MRI findings in my chart.

## Closing request

I respectfully ask MVP to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-13 (Reference number POC-5EDC35C98D-81118) and authorize CPT 29881 as requested by Duval, MD. In the alternative, I ask that MVP identify in writing the exact criterion applied and explain which documented element of my conservative care it found insufficient, so that my surgeon and I can respond to it directly.

**Appeal timing and submission:** My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-09**, and I am submitting this letter within that period. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if another address is required for member appeals, I have been advised to call the number on the back of my insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed, and I ask that MVP redirect this letter internally if needed so it is not delayed.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing. I am happy to supply anything further you need, including the physical therapy discharge note, the MRI report, and my surgeon's office notes.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at my records.

Sincerely,

**Cameron Brooks**
Member ID: W412154328
[My signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures (please confirm what you already have on file):**
- Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-04-08 to 2026-07-15
- MRI of the knee, 2026-07-02
- Office notes from Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-13

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
